items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Henry Ross; the interviewer mentions him in the context of 'Cripple Pill' (who was in Charlie Galloway's band, which the interviewee played in). The interviewee does not confirm a personal relationship with Henry Ross.

ctx.x: I played guitar with Charlie Galloway for a while, not too long. I believe I played with his band about two, three years. That's about all. Charlie Galloway was a bass player and he was the leader of the band. He had one leg, walked with a crutch. And he had a good Dixieland band, jazz band. And I played, I remember playing with him a while, you know. Was he an older man than you or younger? Oh yeah, he was, uh, he was younger than me. Yeah. Who was in his band? Well, uh, they had, uh, some of the old fellas out…

Cripple Pill. Oh yeah. He would have told us about Cripple Pill, uh, uh, Henry Ross. Henry Ross. I didn't know his right name, but all we know was Pill. Crowback? Yeah. They're called him Crowback, too. That's the same guy? And, uh, uh, uh, uh. Were there any other? Oh, go ahead. Let's see this boy's name now. A guitar player. A famous guitar player. He was a golf, uh, uh, uh, can't think of his name.

Well, I wanted to ask you something, now that you mention it. About what color was Brock Mumford? Remember Jeff Mumford from Uptown? Jeff Mumford? Jeff Mumford? Jeff Mumford? Brock. Brock Mumford. Yeah, he was a guitar player.
